newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast prods drop in line with NYMEX fall.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast prods drop in line with NYMEX fall.

text.p: Sellers of U.S. West Coast spot products slashed offers midday Thursday, in line with lower futures markets, traders said.

Overall prices fell 2.00 to 3.00 cents a gallon after West Coast sellers jumped into the market early. They were concerned about a drop in July deliveries of crude oil, which fell as much as 65 cents a barrel on NYMEX.
"It's pressure from the NYMEX and crude in particular," one broker said.
Refined products futures also fell, with July unleaded gasoline 58.70 cents a gallon, off 0.72 cents at 1444 EDT. Heating oil futures slid 0.76 cents a gallon to 53.40 cents.
Offers of Los Angeles regular CARB-grade cleaner burning gasoline dropped two cents to 60 cents a gallon Thursday.
San Francisco CARB gasoline was pegged about two cents gallon lower as well, and fell one cent under LA grades.
Prompt regular unleaded gasoline in Los Angeles was offered at 57.50 cents, 1.50 cents cents lower than Wednesday, traders said.
CARB diesel fuel slid three cents a gallon to 60/61 cents.
